pains.title: A full schedule and thin profit
pains.problem: Payers set the fee for each visit while staff costs keep growing. A busy schedule can still leave little profit.
pains.how: Lucid builds monthly books with margin by location or provider. A CFO review shows which costs outgrow collections and models a new hire before you make it.

pains.title: Payer rates and slow payment hit your bank first
pains.problem: Medicare, Medicaid and a few commercial plans each pay on their own schedule and fee table.
pains.how: Lucid reconciles every payer deposit and tracks payer mix. A cash forecast shows what slower payment does to your cash. Your biller works the claims.

pains.title: Capitation and membership payments are hard to track
pains.problem: Per member and membership money arrives as lump deposits, so a bank feed cannot show what was earned or for which month.
pains.how: Lucid reconciles every deposit and reports by provider. Your CPA advises on the tax treatment of membership money, and your attorney advises on the paperwork.

faq.q: Why is my primary care practice busy but not making money?
faq.a: Payment per visit is set by the payer while staff, rent, malpractice and software costs keep rising, so a full schedule can still leave little profit. Lucid builds a monthly report with live profit and loss by location or provider, then reviews it with you so you see which costs are growing faster than revenue.

faq.q: How do I know which insurance companies are hurting my cash flow?
faq.a: You need collections tracked by payer, not one revenue number. Lucid reconciles every payer deposit and tracks payer mix, so you see which payers pay you less over time. That gives you facts to bring to your biller or to a payer conversation.

faq.q: How should a primary care practice account for capitation and per member payments?
faq.a: Track them apart from visit revenue and match them to the period they cover, so you can see if the arrangement is profitable. Lucid reconciles every deposit, and your dedicated CPA advises on how to treat membership fees paid up front, so you can see what you earned, not just what landed in the bank.

faq.q: How long should it take to get paid by insurance?
faq.a: It varies by payer, so the useful number is your own, tracked over time. Lucid shows payer mix and a cash forecast built on how you actually get paid. Your biller follows up on claims. Lucid does not file or chase them.

faq.q: How much salary should I pay myself from my own practice?
faq.a: It depends on your entity, your profit and what the IRS treats as reasonable pay for your role. Lucid reviews your numbers, helps set a salary you can defend to the IRS and plans your quarterly taxes around real cash flow. Your attorney handles entity and partnership agreements.
